text: After this you can keep an audit review focused, recorded and actionable.

The audit chair manages the process rather than privately deciding technical facts. The meeting should confirm scope, review evidence, distinguish open questions from findings and record decisions from authorized roles. Good minutes say what was examined, what remains uncertain and who will provide the missing proof. Disagreements may reveal different assumptions. Keep the issue visible until it is resolved.

items: Confirm participants, scope and expected output. You should see: Reviewers know what the meeting will decide. If not: Escalate scope or authority disagreements.
Present the accepted configuration and supporting evidence. You should see: All participants use the same reference. If not: Pause on missing or conflicting records.
Record each finding with its evidence and consequence. You should see: The record is understandable later. If not: Separate an observation from a proven nonconformance.
Read back decisions, owners and follow-up dates. You should see: No material issue is left as an informal promise. If not: Correct unclear action wording before closing.
Inferred: An engineer accepts a module, but a technician identifies another revision. Record the mismatch and required evidence. Do not vote on the facts.

text: The chair protects a reliable decision trail.
A meeting cannot authorize changes outside the designated decision process.

items: Leaving the meeting with only a slide deck It may not identify owners and open actions. Fix: Publish controlled minutes and an action register.
